title: Schedule opens from the top-level navigation into a sidebar + grid layout
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser (window at least 960px wide).
2. Your role has the Schedule: View permission (and Work Orders: View, so the sidebar work order list loads).
custom_steps:
1. Look at the app's main (top-level) navigation.
2. Click the Schedule item.
3. Look at the two regions of the Schedule screen.
custom_expected:
1. Schedule is listed as a top-level navigation item alongside Work Orders, Customers, Parts, and Reports.
2. Clicking it opens the Schedule screen.
3. The left panel is the work order sidebar: a mini calendar at the top and a work order list beneath it.
4. The main area is the schedule grid showing technician rows, with a toolbar above it.

title: Day / Week / Month segmented control switches the grid between the three views
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page.
3. At least one shift exists on the current week (create one first if needed, or have a colleague with Edit permission create it).
custom_steps:
1. In the grid toolbar, click Day on the Day / Week / Month segmented control.
2. Click Week.
3. Click Month.
custom_expected:
1. Day: the grid shows a 24-hour timeline per technician row, with shifts positioned at their times.
2. Week: the grid shows a 7-column Monday-to-Sunday layout with stacked shift chips per cell.
3. Month: the grid shows a compact calendar with per-day capacity bars and shift chips.
4. The same shifts remain visible (appropriately rendered) in all three views.

title: Grid rows are grouped by department under group headers, with the department's technicians listed beneath
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. Staff members are assigned to at least two different departments (adjust staff records if needed, restore after).
  3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Read the technician rows in the grid from top to bottom.
  2. Note how the rows are grouped.
custom_expected:
1. Rows are grouped by department, each group under its own header (for example a services group and an administration group - the actual names come from the shop's own departments).
  2. Each department's technicians are listed beneath that department's header.
  3. Every staff member assigned to a visible department appears as a row, regardless of their role.

title: Collapsing a department group header hides its technician rows; expanding restores them
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page with at least one department group visible containing technicians.
custom_steps:
1. Click a department group header to collapse it.
2. Click the same header again to expand it.
custom_expected:
1. Collapsing hides that department's technician rows (the group header stays visible).
2. Expanding shows the technician rows again, unchanged.
3. Other department groups are unaffected.

title: There is no separate technician-only view or Tech/Dept toggle - department grouping is the only grid grouping
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps: 1. Look through the grid toolbar and its dropdowns for any control that switches the grid between a department-grouped view and a flat technician-only view.
custom_expected:
1. No such toggle exists - the department-grouped rows are the only grid grouping.
  2. Department visibility is controlled only through the department toggles in the 'Filter and Display' dropdown.

title: An Unassigned row sits within the grid (not a separate tray) and holds shifts not yet tied to a technician
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. You are on the Schedule page.
  3. At least one unassigned shift exists (a user with Edit permission drops a work order onto the Unassigned row first).
custom_steps:
1. Look for the unassigned row inside the schedule grid.
  2. Note where the unassigned shift is displayed.
custom_expected:
1. An unassigned row/lane appears within the grid itself - it is not a separate tray or panel outside the grid.
  2. Shifts without a technician sit in this row.
  3. The unassigned shift uses the same block layout as regular shifts (customer, unit, line name / line count) - it simply has no technician.

title: Clicking a date in the mini calendar navigates the main grid to that date
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. You are on the Schedule page with the mini calendar visible in the left sidebar.
custom_steps:
1. In the mini calendar, click a date in a different week from the one currently shown in the grid.
  2. Look at the main grid and its date label.
custom_expected:
1. The main grid navigates to show the clicked date (the containing day/week/month depending on the active view).
  2. The toolbar date label updates to the new range.
  3. The clicked date is highlighted as the selected date in the mini calendar.

title: Mini calendar month/year picker offers a grid of month buttons and year navigation arrows
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the mini calendar visible.
custom_steps:
1. Open the mini calendar's month/year picker.
2. Use the year arrows to move to another year.
3. Pick a different month from the grid of month buttons.
custom_expected:
1. A picker opens showing a grid of month buttons plus arrows to step the year back and forward.
2. Choosing a month shows that month in the mini calendar.
3. The main grid can then be navigated by clicking a date in the newly shown month.

title: A chevron toggle collapses and expands the mini calendar grid
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the mini calendar expanded.
custom_steps:
1. Click the chevron toggle on the mini calendar.
2. Look at the sidebar.
3. Click the chevron again.
custom_expected:
1. The calendar grid collapses (hides), leaving more room for the work order list below.
2. Clicking again expands the calendar grid back.

title: Mini calendar highlights the selected date, indicates today, and highlights the week row on hover
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the mini calendar visible.
3. The grid is on a date other than today (click a different date first).
custom_steps:
1. Look at the mini calendar and find today's date and the selected date.
2. Move the mouse over different week rows of the mini calendar.
custom_expected:
1. The selected date is visually highlighted.
2. Today's date has its own distinct indicator, different from the selection.
3. Hovering a week row highlights that whole week row.

title: The sidebar shows a flat, scrollable list of work order cards with no Assigned/Unassigned tabs
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: View and Work Orders: View.
  2. Several open work orders exist (create ZZAUTOTEST work orders if needed).
  3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the work order list beneath the mini calendar.
  2. Scroll the list.
  3. Look for any Assigned/Unassigned tabs above the list.
custom_expected:
1. Work orders appear as a single flat list of cards (one list, no tab split).
  2. The list scrolls when there are more cards than fit.
  3. There are no Assigned/Unassigned tabs - assignment is available only as a filter behind the 'Filter' button.

title: Work order card shows WO number, line count plus hours, customer, unit, lead technician, and a status-colored left border
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A work order exists with a customer, a unit, at least one approved line with estimated hours, and a lead technician assigned.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Find that work order's card in the sidebar list.
2. Read the card from top to bottom.
custom_expected:
1. Top left: the work order number, shown in an accent color.
2. Top right: the line count plus the hours estimate.
3. Below: the customer name in bold, then the unit number.
4. A lead technician row with the technician's avatar and name.
5. A colored left border whose color reflects the work order's status.

title: 'Search work orders' matches work order number, customer, unit, and technician
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Work orders exist with different work order numbers and with distinct customer names, unit numbers, and lead technicians.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Click the 'Search work orders' field at the top of the list and type the number of one specific work order; note the results, then clear.
2. Type part of a customer name; note the results, then clear.
3. Type a unit number; note the results, then clear.
4. Type a technician's name; note the results.
custom_expected:
1. Work-order-number search narrows the list to the card(s) whose work order number matches what you typed, and cards that do not match disappear.
2. Customer-name search shows only cards for that customer.
3. Unit-number search shows only cards with that unit.
4. Technician-name search shows only cards where that technician appears on the card.
5. All four searchable fields (WO number, customer, unit, technician) are fields visible on the card itself.

title: Sidebar search filters the card list in real time as you type
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Several work orders exist.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Type a search term into 'Search work orders' one character at a time.
2. Watch the list while typing (do not press Enter).
custom_expected:
1. The list narrows live with each keystroke - no Enter press or apply button is needed.
2. Deleting characters widens the results again.
3. With very many work orders, the list may load further results in pages as you scroll - that is expected, not a fault.

title: Sidebar search with no matching work orders shows an empty list
refs: SV-8687 (§3.1 (derived - search behavior with no matches))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. In 'Search work orders', type a nonsense string that matches nothing (for example 'zzzxq999').
2. Look at the list.
3. Clear the search.
custom_expected:
1. No work order cards are shown.
2. The app does not error; the sidebar remains usable.
3. Clearing the search restores the full list.

title: The 'Filters' button opens Assignment / Status / Priority filter groups
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Several work orders exist in mixed statuses and priorities.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Click the 'Filters' button on the sidebar.
2. Read the filter groups offered.
3. Apply one filter option and look at the 'Filters' button.
custom_expected:
1. The filter panel offers three groups: Assignment (Assigned, Unassigned), Status (the work order statuses supported in the app), and Priority (High, Medium, Low).
2. Applying a filter narrows the flat card list.
3. The 'Filters' button shows a badge with the number of active filters.

title: Assignment filter narrows the list to Assigned or Unassigned work orders
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. At least one work order has a technician assigned and at least one has none.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Open the 'Filter' panel and choose Unassigned under Assignment.
2. Read the list.
3. Switch to Assigned and read the list again.
custom_expected:
1. Unassigned: only work orders without an assigned technician remain in the list.
2. Assigned: only work orders with a technician assigned remain.
3. There are no Assigned/Unassigned tabs - this filter is the only assignment split.

title: Status filter narrows the list to work orders in the chosen status(es)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Work orders exist in at least two different statuses.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Open the 'Filter' panel.
2. Choose one status under Status.
3. Read the list.
custom_expected:
1. The Status group lists the work order statuses the app supports.
2. Only work orders in the chosen status remain in the card list.
3. The card left-border colors of the remaining cards are consistent with that status.

title: Priority filter offers High, Medium, Low and narrows the list accordingly
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Work orders exist with different priorities (High and Low at minimum).
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Open the 'Filter' panel.
2. Choose High under Priority.
3. Read the list.
custom_expected:
1. The Priority group offers High, Medium, and Low.
2. Only High-priority work orders remain in the list.

title: 'Clear all' resets every applied sidebar filter in one click
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page and have applied at least two filters (for example an Assignment and a Priority filter).
custom_steps:
1. Click 'Clear all'.
2. Look at the list and the 'Filter' button.
custom_expected:
1. All applied filters are removed at once.
2. The full work order list is shown again.
3. The active-count badge on the 'Filter' button disappears (or shows zero).

title: Search and filter work together - both can be active at the same time
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Several work orders exist for the same customer in different statuses.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Type a customer name into 'Search work orders'.
2. With the search still applied, open 'Filter' and choose one status.
3. Read the list.
custom_expected:
1. The list shows only work orders that match BOTH the text search and the structured filter.
2. Removing either the search text or the filter widens the list to the remaining condition.

title: Work order card opens the line drill-down in place, with header and back control
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A work order exists with a known number of approved lines (at least two).
3. You are on the Schedule page with the work order list visible.
custom_steps:
1. Click that work order's card in the sidebar.
2. Look at the sidebar.
3. Read the header of the drill-down.
4. Click the back control.
custom_expected:
1. The card list is replaced, in the same place, by that work order's lines (no new page or popup).
2. The header of the drill-down shows the work order id.
3. The header also shows the line count, and it matches the number of approved lines.
4. A back control is shown to return to the card list.
5. Clicking back restores the work order card list.

title: Only approved work order lines appear in the drill-down - unapproved lines are not shown
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists with at least one APPROVED line and at least one UNAPPROVED line (create/adjust it first).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open that work order's drill-down in the sidebar.
2. Compare the lines listed against the work order's actual lines.
custom_expected:
1. Every approved line is listed.
2. The unapproved line does NOT appear anywhere in the schedule sidebar.
3. The header's line count matches the approved lines only.

title: Each line row shows its title, estimated hours, technician roster (avatar stack plus count, no cap), and a drag handle
refs: SV-8687 (§3.1 (Line drill-down),§8.1 (Line labor roster - no cap))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists whose approved lines have estimated hours; at least one line has several technicians on its roster.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the drill-down open.
custom_steps:
1. Read one line row.
2. Look at a line with multiple technicians on it.
custom_expected:
1. The row shows the line's title and its estimated hours.
2. The current technician roster is shown as an avatar stack plus a count; there is no cap on how many technicians a line can have.
3. Each line row has its own drag handle, so it can be dragged independently onto the grid.

title: Lines with no technician assigned show a 'Needs techs' badge
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A work order exists with an approved line that has NO technician on its roster and another approved line that has at least one.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the drill-down open.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the line with no technician.
2. Look at the line that has a technician.
custom_expected:
1. The technician-less line shows a 'Needs techs' badge.
2. The line with a technician does not show the badge.
3. After a technician is scheduled onto the badge-bearing line, the badge goes away.

title: 'Search lines' matches the line title/name only
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A work order exists with several approved lines with distinct titles.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the drill-down open.
custom_steps:
1. In the drill-down's line search box, type part of one line's title.
2. Read the results.
3. Clear it and type the customer's name instead.
custom_expected:
1. Typing a line title narrows the list to matching lines.
2. Typing the customer name returns no results - the line search matches line titles only (the list is already scoped to one work order, so customer/unit/WO fields are not searched).

title: 'All / Unscheduled' filter chips with counts - Unscheduled shows only lines with no shifts yet
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A work order exists where at least one approved line already has a shift on the grid and at least one approved line has none.
3. You are on the Schedule page with the drill-down open.
custom_steps:
1. Read the two filter chips and their counts.
2. Click the Unscheduled chip.
3. Click the All chip.
custom_expected:
1. Two chips are shown - All and Unscheduled - each with a count.
2. Unscheduled lists only the lines that have no shifts yet, and its count matches.
3. All lists every approved line, and its count matches the drill-down header's line count.

title: Dropping a single-line work order on a technician cell creates a shift immediately, skipping the scope picker
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
  2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists with exactly ONE approved line whose estimated hours fit within one working day of the target technician.
  3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag that work order's card from the sidebar.
  2. Drop it onto a technician's cell on a working day.
custom_expected:
1. A shift is created immediately in that cell - no scope picker and no spread step appears.
  2. The shift block shows the customer name, unit number, and the line's name.
  3. The technician is added to that line's labor roster on the work order.
  4. A toast with an Undo option appears.

title: Dropping a multi-line work order on a technician cell opens the scope picker
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with TWO or more approved lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag that work order's card from the sidebar.
2. Drop it onto a technician's cell.
custom_expected:
1. A scope picker popover opens, anchored to the cell you dropped on.
2. It offers 'Schedule whole work order' at the top, the individual line rows beneath, and a 'Select multiple' control.
3. No shift is created until a scope is chosen.

title: Dragging an individual line from the drill-down creates a single-line shift directly
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order with several approved lines exists; its drill-down is open in the sidebar.
3. The chosen line's hours fit within one working day of the target technician.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Using the line's drag handle, drag one specific line from the drill-down.
2. Drop it onto a technician's cell.
custom_expected:
1. A single-line shift for exactly that line is created directly - no scope picker appears.
2. The block's last text line shows that line's name.
3. The technician is added to that line's roster only (not to the order's other lines).

title: A job exceeding the technician's daily hours opens the spread step after the scope is chosen
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists whose chosen scope's estimated hours EXCEED one working day of the target technician (for example a 40h line for a tech with 8h days).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the work order (or the large line) onto a technician's cell.
2. If the scope picker opens, choose the large scope.
3. Look at what opens next.
custom_expected:
1. The spread step opens (step 2 of the same modal) to distribute the hours across consecutive working days.
2. Its header shows the chosen scope and a 'Change scope' back-link.
3. No shifts exist yet until the spread is confirmed.

title: A scope that fits within one working day skips the spread step and creates a single shift
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists where one line's hours fit within the target technician's working day.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. In the scope picker, tap the small line.
custom_expected:
1. The shift is created straight away - the spread step does NOT appear.
2. The shift sits on the dropped day only.

title: While dragging, drop-target cells highlight and a ghost block shows the line name and hours
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order with an approved line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Start dragging a line from the sidebar and hold it over different grid cells without dropping.
2. Watch the cell under the cursor and the dragged preview.
custom_expected:
1. The cell currently under the cursor highlights as a drop target.
2. A ghost block follows the drag showing the line name and its hours.
3. Releasing outside any valid cell creates nothing.

title: Scheduling a technician onto a line adds them to that line's labor roster on the work order
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with an approved line where the target technician is NOT yet on the line's roster.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Drag that line onto the technician's cell and create the shift.
2. Open the same work order's line (in the sidebar drill-down and/or on the Work Orders page) and check its technician roster.
custom_expected:
1. The technician now appears on that line's labor roster - the schedule and the work order stay in sync automatically.
2. The sidebar line row's avatar stack/count updates to include the technician.
3. If the line previously showed 'Needs techs', the badge is gone.

title: A click-to-arm alternative exists for scheduling without dragging
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order with an approved line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Instead of dragging, click (arm) the work order card or line in the sidebar.
2. Then click a technician cell in the grid.
custom_expected:
1. The item can be placed onto a cell without holding a drag - clicking arms it, and clicking a cell places it.
2. The result is the same as the equivalent drag-and-drop (scope picker / spread step rules apply the same way).

title: Scope picker contents: the pinned whole-order row and the line rows
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with three approved lines with known estimated hours, where at least one line already has technicians on its roster.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell to open the scope picker.
2. Read the top option.
3. Read each line row below it.
custom_expected:
1. The 'Schedule whole work order' option sits pinned at the top of the picker and looks visually distinct from the line rows.
2. It is labeled with the order's line count and total hours (matching the sum of the approved lines).
3. The picker is anchored to the cell that was dropped on.
4. Each line row shows the line title and its estimated hours.
5. Rows for lines that already have technicians show the current roster as an avatar stack plus count.

title: Choosing 'Schedule whole work order' assigns the technician to all lines and creates one whole-order shift
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST work order exists with two or more approved lines whose TOTAL hours fit within the technician's working day (to avoid the spread step).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. Choose 'Schedule whole work order'.
3. Check the created block and the work order's line rosters.
custom_expected:
1. One shift is created covering all of the order's approved lines.
2. The block's last text line reads 'N Lines' (with N = the line count).
3. The technician is added to the roster of every one of those lines.

title: Tapping an individual line row immediately creates a single-line shift with no confirmation step
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists; one line fits within the technician's day.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. In the scope picker, click one line row (do not use 'Select multiple').
custom_expected:
1. A single-line shift for that line is created immediately - no extra confirmation step.
2. The picker closes.
3. The block's last text line shows the line's name.

title: 'Select multiple' checkbox mode: running tally, Select all, and Cancel
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order exists with three or more approved lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the work order onto a technician's cell.
2. Click 'Select multiple'.
3. Tick two lines and read the confirm bar.
4. Click 'Select all' and read the tally.
5. Click Cancel instead of confirming, and look at the picker.
6. Re-open 'Select multiple', tick two lines again, and confirm.
custom_expected:
1. The line rows switch into checkbox mode.
2. A confirm bar appears with a running tally of the selection - the count of lines and their combined hours (in the spec's example format, 'Create shift · 2 lines · 6h').
3. 'Select all' ticks every line - the tally equals the whole order (same line count and hours as 'Schedule whole work order').
4. Cancel leaves checkbox mode and returns to the normal single-tap line list without creating anything.
5. Confirming creates ONE shift covering the ticked lines, and the technician is added to those lines' rosters only.

title: A shift's start time uses the technician's configured working hours when they are set
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
  2. A technician has configured working hours that DIFFER from the shop's business hours (for example tech 6:00 AM start vs shop 8:00 AM) - set this up first and restore after.
  3. A schedulable work order line exists.
  4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell (week view - not a day-view timeline drop).
  2. Open the created shift's detail and read its start time.
custom_expected: 1. The shift starts at the technician's own configured start time (6:00 AM in the example), not the shop's business-hours start.

title: With no technician hours set, the shift start time falls back to the shop's business hours
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician exists with NO configured working hours, and the shop HAS business hours set (note the shop start time).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell.
2. Read the created shift's start time.
custom_expected: 1. The shift starts at the shop's business-hours start time.

title: With neither technician hours nor business hours set, a 7:00 AM default applies
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician exists with no configured hours AND the shop's business hours are not set (adjust settings if the environment allows; restore the settings byte-identical after).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell.
2. Read the created shift's start time.
custom_expected: 1. The shift starts at 7:00 AM - the general default working day (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM) applies.

title: In day view, the start time comes from where the shift is dropped on the timeline
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A schedulable work order line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the line from the sidebar and drop it at a specific time position on a technician's timeline (for example around 10:00 AM).
2. Read the created shift's start time.
custom_expected:
1. The shift starts at the time position where it was dropped (not at the technician-hours/business-hours default).
2. The start time aligns to the timeline position (see the 15-minute snapping case).

title: Dropping a work order or line onto the Unassigned row creates an unassigned shift with no technician
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A schedulable work order line exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the line from the sidebar and drop it onto the grid's Unassigned row on a working day.
2. Look at the created block and the line's roster.
custom_expected:
1. An unassigned shift is created in the Unassigned row for that day.
2. It has no technician (and no technician is added to the line's roster by this drop).
3. The block uses the same anatomy as a regular shift (customer, unit, line name / 'N Lines').

title: Unassigned shift start time skips the technician-hours rule and uses business hours or the default
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. The shop has business hours set (note the start time).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the line onto the Unassigned row.
2. Read the created shift's start time.
custom_expected: 1. The unassigned shift starts at the shop's business-hours start (there is no technician whose hours could apply).

title: Dragging an unassigned shift onto a technician row assigns it, and that technician's hours then apply
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. An unassigned shift exists in the Unassigned row.
3. The target technician has configured working hours that differ from the shop's business hours.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the unassigned shift from the Unassigned row down onto a technician's row.
2. Check the shift and the line's roster.
custom_expected:
1. The shift is now assigned to that technician (it leaves the Unassigned row and sits in the technician's row).
2. The technician is added to the affected line's roster.
3. The technician's own working hours now apply to the shift's timing.

title: Spread step header shows the scope; 'Change scope' returns to the picker
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A multi-line work order exists with a scope that exceeds the technician's daily hours.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the work order on a technician, choose the large scope, and reach the spread step.
2. Read the spread step's header.
3. Click 'Change scope'.
4. Choose a different scope and continue.
custom_expected:
1. The spread step appears as step 2 of the same modal.
2. Its header shows the chosen scope (which lines / how many hours).
3. A 'Change scope' back-link is present.
4. Clicking 'Change scope' takes the modal back to the scope picker (step 1) without creating anything.
5. Choosing a new scope updates the spread step's header and hours accordingly.

title: How-much selector defaults to Full estimate; Full estimate, 1 week, and 2 weeks apply immediately with no extra fields
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a large scope (for example 40+ hours).
custom_steps:
1. Read the 'how much to schedule' selector's default value.
2. Open the selector and read its options.
3. Pick '1 week', then '2 weeks', then back to 'Full estimate', watching for extra fields.
custom_expected:
1. The selector defaults to 'Full estimate'.
2. The options include 'Full estimate', '1 week', '2 weeks', 'Until a date…', and 'Specific hours…'.
3. 'Full estimate', '1 week', and '2 weeks' apply on selection with no extra fields - the modal stays to one line for these.
4. The preview summary updates to match each selection.

title: 'Until a date…' reveals a single finish-by date field
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a large scope.
custom_steps:
1. Open the how-much selector and choose 'Until a date…'.
2. Look at the modal.
3. Pick a finish-by date.
custom_expected:
1. Choosing 'Until a date…' reveals a single 'finish by' date field (this is the only custom control shown).
2. Picking a date updates the preview so the series ends by that date.

title: 'Specific hours…' reveals an hours stepper
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a large scope.
custom_steps:
1. Open the how-much selector and choose 'Specific hours…'.
2. Set a number of hours with the stepper (for example 16).
custom_expected:
1. Choosing 'Specific hours…' reveals an hours stepper control.
2. The preview updates to spread exactly the entered hours across working days.

title: Start date defaults to the earliest working day and can be adjusted to make a second technician sequential
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A large job has already been spread for technician A (note A's series end date).
3. You are on the spread step for the SAME work order dropped on technician B.
custom_steps:
1. Read the start-date field's default.
2. Change the start date to the day after technician A's series ends.
3. Confirm the spread.
custom_expected:
1. The start date defaults to the earliest working day.
2. It can be changed; technician B's series then starts after A's series ends (sequential, not parallel).
3. B's series is created from the adjusted start date onward.

title: Spread uses the tech's working hours; skips weekends only when hours not set
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. The technician has known daily working hours (for example 8h/day, Monday to Friday).
3. A shop closure day is defined inside the spread window (set one up if the environment allows).
4. A scope of known size exists (for example 40h).
custom_steps:
1. Spread the 40h scope for that technician with 'Full estimate' starting on a Monday.
2. Confirm and inspect the created shifts on the grid.
custom_expected:
1. Daily shifts are sized to the technician's own working hours (8h each in the example).
2. Weekends are skipped ONLY when the technician has no business hours set for them; if the tech has hours on a weekend day (e.g. Saturday hours) that day is NOT skipped.
3. Shop closures and public holidays are NOT skipped in V1 - shifts can be placed on those days.
4. The end date is a result of the daily distribution (for 40h at 8h/day starting Monday, the series ends on the fifth working day).

title: Preview is collapsed to a one-line summary, expandable to a week-by-week breakdown with skipped days struck through and their reasons
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a multi-week scope that will skip at least one weekend.
custom_steps:
1. Read the preview area without expanding it.
2. Expand the preview.
3. Find a skipped day in the breakdown.
custom_expected:
1. Collapsed: a one-line summary in the spirit of the spec's example '20 shifts · Jun 15 to Jul 13 · skips weekends + 2 days'.
2. Expanded: a week-by-week breakdown of the planned shifts.
3. Skipped days are struck through and show the reason they are skipped - in V1 the only skip reason is a weekend day with no working hours set.

title: Confirming the spread creates a linked series of daily shifts
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the spread step for a multi-day scope with the preview showing several shifts.
custom_steps:
1. Confirm the spread.
2. Look at the grid across the affected days/weeks.
3. Open one of the created shifts.
custom_expected:
1. One daily shift is created per planned working day, together forming a linked series.
2. The shifts render as one connected banner (see the series-banner cases).
3. Each daily shift keeps its own day and hours.
4. A toast with Undo appears.

title: Dropping the same work order on a second technician spreads the full estimate again, independently
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A large work order (for example 40h) has already been fully spread for technician A.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the SAME work order onto technician B and complete the spread with 'Full estimate'.
2. Compare the two series.
custom_expected:
1. Technician B gets a full 40h series of their own - the estimate is spread again in full, not reduced by A's booking.
2. There is no shared 'remaining hours' counter across technicians and no splitting of a shift.
3. Planned hours across technicians may now exceed the estimate - this is expected and produces no error (progress is driven by clocked-in time).

title: Spread past 8 weeks asks to confirm; a series can never exceed 120 shifts
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A work order line with a very large hours estimate exists (enough to fill more than 8 weeks of daily shifts - seed one if needed).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the large job onto a technician and reach the spread step.
2. Choose a spread that runs longer than 8 weeks (about 2 months) and try to confirm.
3. Read the message that appears, then confirm/acknowledge it and continue.
4. Now try an extreme spread that would create more than 120 daily shifts in one go (raise the hours or extend the finish-by date) and try to confirm.
custom_expected:
1. Going past 8 weeks does not silently succeed: a warning about the very long series appears and asks you to confirm before the shifts are created.
2. After you confirm the warning, the long series is created normally.
3. A single spread that would create more than 120 daily shifts is refused outright - no confirmation can override it, and no shifts are created for that attempt.
4. No half-created series is left behind after a refused attempt.

title: Month view: series banner wraps across weeks, labeled once, then 'continues'
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-week series exists for one technician (spread a 40h+ job first).
3. You are on the Schedule page in MONTH view showing the series' month.
custom_steps:
1. Find the series on the month grid.
2. Read the banner across the week rows.
3. Look at the weekend columns inside the series.
custom_expected:
1. The series renders as one continuous bar wrapping across the week rows.
2. It is labeled once at the start (including the technician); later weeks show a faded 'continues'-style label instead of repeating the full label.
3. Weekend columns inside the series are empty (no bar) when no business hours are set for those weekend days.

title: Week view: series banner spans the week, with chevrons and 'week N of M'
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-week series exists for one technician; on one of its days the technician also has an unrelated booking.
3. You are on the Schedule page in WEEK view on a middle week of the series.
custom_steps:
1. Find the series banner in the technician's row.
2. Look at the banner's left and right edges.
3. Look for the week-position cue and at the day with the other booking.
custom_expected:
1. One banner spans the working days of that week in the technician's row.
2. Chevrons at the banner's edges indicate the series continues beyond the visible week (both sides, on a middle week).
3. A 'week N of M' cue shows the position within the series.

title: Day view shows the series day as a single time-positioned block with a 'part of an M-week job' cue
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-week series exists for one technician.
3. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view on one of the series' days.
custom_steps:
1. Find the series' block on the technician's timeline.
2. Read its cue text.
custom_expected:
1. The day shows a single time-positioned block (no spanning bar - only one day is visible).
2. The block carries a cue in the spirit of 'part of an M-week job' indicating it belongs to a longer series.

title: A series is a grouping of ordinary daily shifts - capacity, overtime, and conflicts operate on the individual shifts
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A series exists for a technician; on one series day the technician also has a second, overlapping shift (set up with Edit permission).
3. Capacity Bars are on in View Options.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the capacity bar of a day inside the series.
2. Look at the day with the overlapping second shift.
3. Open one series shift's detail.
custom_expected:
1. Each series day contributes its own daily hours to that day's capacity bar (the series is not counted as one lump).
2. The overlapping day is flagged as a Double-booked conflict, exactly as it would be for standalone shifts.
3. The detail modal shows that single day's shift (its own day and hours) while indicating it belongs to the series.

title: A single-line shift block shows three text lines: customer name, unit number, and the line name
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. A single-line shift exists on the grid (VIN toggle off).
  3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps: 1. Read the shift block's text lines from top to bottom.
custom_expected:
1. Line 1: the customer name.
  2. Line 2: the unit number.
  3. Last line: the name of the scheduled line.
  4. No work order number appears on the block.

title: Whole-order and multi-line-subset shifts both read 'N Lines' on the block - the detail modal spells out the exact scope
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Two shifts exist for a 4-line work order: one whole-order shift (4 lines) and one 2-line subset shift.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Read the last text line of the whole-order shift's block.
2. Read the last text line of the subset shift's block.
3. Open each shift's detail modal.
custom_expected:
1. The whole-order block reads '4 Lines'.
2. The subset block reads '2 Lines' - the block does not distinguish whole-order from subset beyond the count.
3. Each detail modal lists exactly which lines the shift covers.

title: The conflict icon is the only icon on a shift block - no work order number and no scope icons
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. One normal (unconflicted) shift and one conflicted shift exist (create an overlapping second shift to force a conflict).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Inspect the unconflicted block for icons and a work order number.
2. Inspect the conflicted block.
custom_expected:
1. The unconflicted block shows NO icons and NO work order number - only its text lines.
2. The conflicted block shows the conflict (warning) icon on its first line - and that is the only icon that ever appears on a block.
3. No scope icons distinguish whole-order from subset shifts.

title: Non-overlapping same-day shifts share one lane, even from different orders
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Two DIFFERENT work orders have schedulable lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Schedule a shift from work order 1 onto a technician for a given day (for example 8:00-10:00).
2. Schedule a shift from work order 2 onto the SAME technician for the SAME day at a non-overlapping time (for example 10:00-12:00).
3. Switch to day view and look at the technician's row on that day.
custom_expected:
1. Both shifts are created and shown on the same day for the same technician - multiple same-day shifts from different work orders are allowed.
2. Both shifts sit in the same single lane, one after the other.
3. The row stays at its normal height.
4. No conflict is flagged for back-to-back (non-intersecting) shifts.

title: Shifts whose times intersect split into stacked lanes and the row grows to fit
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. One technician has two shifts on the same day whose time ranges DO intersect (for example 9:00-12:00 and 10:00-13:00).
3. You are on the Schedule page in day view.
custom_steps: 1. Look at the technician's row on that day.
custom_expected:
1. The two overlapping shifts render in separate stacked lanes - they never visually collide.
2. The row grows in height to fit the lanes.
3. The overlap is also flagged as a Double-booked conflict (stacking reads as 'resolve me').

title: Visible lanes cap at 3 - additional overlapping shifts collapse into a '+N more' affordance that opens a popover
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. One technician has FIVE mutually overlapping shifts at the same time on the same day (seed ZZAUTOTEST work orders as needed).
3. You are on the Schedule page in day view.
custom_steps:
1. Count the visible lanes in the technician's row.
2. Find and click the '+N more' affordance.
custom_expected:
1. At most 3 lanes are visible.
2. The remaining overlapping shifts collapse into a '+N more' affordance (here '+2 more').
3. Clicking it opens a popover listing the hidden shifts.
4. The hidden shifts can be opened from that popover.

title: Lane stacking and the '+N more' overflow apply in day, week, and month views
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. One technician has several overlapping shifts on the same day.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. View the day in day view and note the stacking/overflow.
2. Switch to week view and look at the same day's cell.
3. Switch to month view and look at the same day.
custom_expected:
1. All three views handle the overlap without blocks visually colliding.
2. Week and month views reach the '+N more' overflow sooner than day view (their cells are narrower), but the same cap-and-overflow model applies.
3. The overflow affordance opens the hidden-shifts popover in each view.

title: Day view auto-scrolls to the working-day start; manual scrolling stands
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Technicians have configured start times; note the EARLIEST one (or the business-hours start / 7:00 AM if none).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Switch to day view and look at where the timeline is scrolled to.
2. Manually scroll the timeline to a late-night hour (for example 11:00 PM).
3. Wait a few seconds and interact with the page without changing the day (hover blocks, open/close a tooltip).
4. Navigate to the next day with the toolbar arrow and look again.
custom_expected:
1. On load and on each day navigation, the timeline is auto-scrolled so the working-day start sits at the left edge of the visible area, with a small buffer (roughly 30 to 60 minutes) before it.
2. The start used is the earliest technician's configured start; if no tech hours are set, business hours; otherwise 7:00 AM - so no shifts sit off-screen to the left.
3. Your manual scroll position stays put - nothing jumps you back to the morning while you remain on the same day.
4. The timeline is not stuck at the start - it remains a full 24-hour scrollable timeline (midnight to midnight).
5. Only navigating to another day re-triggers the auto-scroll.

title: Date and time headers stick to the top of the viewport during vertical scroll (day and week views)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Enough technician rows exist that the grid scrolls vertically.
3. You are on the Schedule page in day view.
custom_steps:
1. Scroll the grid down so lower technician rows come into view.
2. Look at the top of the viewport.
3. Repeat in week view.
custom_expected:
1. In day view, the date/time header bar stays stuck to the top while the rows scroll beneath it - you always know which time column you are looking at.
2. The same sticky-header behavior applies in week view.

title: Dragging a shift horizontally moves its start time, snapping to 15-minute intervals
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift exists on a technician's day-view timeline.
3. You are on the Schedule page in day view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the shift block horizontally along the timeline and release at a position between clean quarter-hours.
2. Open the shift and read its new start time.
3. Undo via the toast if needed and restore the original time.
custom_expected:
1. The shift moves along the timeline as you drag.
2. The released start time snaps to a 15-minute interval (for example 9:15, 9:30 - never 9:22).
3. The duration is unchanged by a horizontal move.
4. A toast with Undo appears for the move.

title: Dragging a shift's left or right edge resizes its duration
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift exists on a technician's day-view timeline (note its start/end).
3. You are on the Schedule page in day view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the shift's RIGHT edge further right and release.
2. Drag the shift's LEFT edge and release.
3. Open the shift and read its times.
custom_expected:
1. Dragging the right edge extends/shortens the end time (start unchanged).
2. Dragging the left edge adjusts the start time (end unchanged).
3. The resulting times land on 15-minute increments.
4. The shift's duration on the grid matches the modal's start/end.

title: A now line marks the current time on today's day view, with a label on hover
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page in day view, on TODAY (click 'Today' if needed).
custom_steps:
1. Scroll the timeline to the current time.
2. Find the vertical current-time indicator.
3. Hover over it.
custom_expected:
1. A vertical line marks the current time on the timeline.
2. Its position matches the actual clock time.
3. Hovering the now line while your pointer is over the grid shows a label (the current time).

title: Clicking a shift opens its detail modal showing customer, unit, VIN (always visible), and the work order id
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. A shift exists for a unit that has a VIN; the VIN toggle in 'Filter and Display' is OFF.
  3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Click the shift block.
  2. Read the modal's identity section.
custom_expected:
1. A detail panel opens for the shift.
  2. It shows the customer name, unit number, the VIN (below unit and asset), and the work order id.
  3. The VIN is visible here even though the grid's VIN toggle is off - the modal always shows it.

title: Scheduled date and start/end time pickers work in 15-minute increments
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift exists; its detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Open the start-time picker and read the available options.
2. Change the start and end times.
3. Change the scheduled date.
4. Check the block on the grid.
custom_expected:
1. The time pickers offer 15-minute increments (for example 8:00, 8:15, 8:30, 8:45).
2. Saving/applying the change updates the shift's times.
3. Changing the date moves the shift to the chosen day.
4. The grid block reflects the new date/times.

title: The modal shows the technician and time logged vs estimate progress
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A shift exists whose line has some clocked-in time logged against an estimate (seed by clocking a technician in/out if possible).
3. The shift's detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Read the technician shown.
2. Read the time-logged vs estimate progress.
custom_expected:
1. The assigned technician is shown.
2. A progress indication compares time logged against the estimate (logged hours vs estimated hours).
3. The numbers are consistent with the line's actual logged time and estimate.

title: The modal shows a scope summary and the scheduled line(s) with number, title, hours, and status only
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-line (subset) shift exists covering 2 of a work order's 4 lines.
3. The shift's detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Read the scope summary.
2. Read the list of scheduled lines and their figures.
custom_expected:
1. The 'Work Order Lines' section shows the line count and a scope summary of what the shift covers.
2. Exactly the 2 scheduled lines are listed (not all 4), each showing its line number, title, hours, and a status pill only.
3. No labor figures and no total dollar amount appear anywhere in the modal.
4. This is where whole-order vs subset scope is spelled out (the grid block only says 'N Lines').

title: Estimated hours can be edited inline in the modal
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift exists; its detail modal is open; note the current estimated hours.
custom_steps:
1. Edit the estimated hours inline (change the value).
2. Confirm/apply the edit.
3. Re-open the modal and read the estimate.
custom_expected:
1. The estimated hours field is editable directly in the modal.
2. The new value persists after closing and re-opening.
3. Dependent displays (progress vs estimate) reflect the new value.

title: Notes can be added, edited, and deleted per work order from the modal
refs: SV-8695 (§4.9 (Notes: add,edit,and delete per work order))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift exists; its detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Add a note (text 'ZZAUTOTEST note').
2. Edit the note's text.
3. Delete the note.
custom_expected:
1. The note is added and shown in the modal.
2. The edit is saved and displayed.
3. The delete removes the note.
4. Notes are kept per work order (the same note is visible from another shift of the same work order).

title: A conflicted shift's modal shows a conflict banner with an 'Adjust' action
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A conflicted shift exists (for example double-booked - create an overlap).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open the conflicted shift's detail modal.
2. Read the banner.
3. Click 'Adjust'.
custom_expected:
1. A conflict banner is shown in the modal describing the conflict.
2. It offers an 'Adjust' action.
3. 'Adjust' leads to a way to resolve the conflict (for example changing the shift's time).
4. An unconflicted shift's modal shows no such banner.

title: Shift modal offers Delete only - there is no Reassign action
refs: SV-8695 (§4.9 (Actions - Delete only; Reassign removed in Confluence v23),§7)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete (which includes Edit and View).
2. A shift exists; its detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the modal's actions.
2. Confirm there is no 'Reassign' action anywhere in the modal.
3. Click Delete on a series shift and read what it asks (cancel without deleting).
custom_expected:
1. The modal offers a Delete action (a trash icon in the header) and a close (x) icon - and no other actions.
2. There is no 'Reassign' action in the modal; reassignment is done by dragging a shift to another technician row (covered by its own case).
3. Delete on a series member asks for a deletion scope (the full scope behavior has its own cases).

title: Create an event via left-click 'Create Event' on empty grid space
refs: SV-8696 (§4.10 (left-click menu on empty grid space),§7)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Left-click an empty spot in a technician's cell on a working day (not on an existing block).
2. Choose 'Create Event' from the menu that opens.
3. Fill in a name (for example 'ZZAUTOTEST stand-up'), keep the date/times offered, and save.
custom_expected:
1. A menu opens at the spot you clicked and contains 'Create Event'.
2. The event modal opens with the clicked cell's technician and date pre-set.
3. Saving creates an event block on that technician's day.
4. A toast with Undo appears.

title: Day view event creation shows a live preview block you can drag to resize
refs: SV-8696 (§4.10 (left-click menu entry; day-view live preview,drag-to-resize))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view.
custom_steps:
1. Left-click an empty spot on a technician's timeline and choose 'Create Event' from the menu that opens.
2. While creating, watch the block and try dragging to size it.
3. Complete the event creation.
custom_expected:
1. Left-clicking empty day-view space opens the cell menu; choosing 'Create Event' starts creation at the time you clicked.
2. A live preview block is shown while creating, and dragging resizes it.
3. Completing creates the event at the previewed time/duration.

title: Event modal fields all save; the all-day toggle creates an all-day event
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the event modal open (left-click empty grid space, then 'Create Event').
custom_steps:
1. Read the fields the modal offers.
2. Fill each: name, date, start and end time, and pick a color category. Save, then re-open the event.
3. Open the event modal again, turn the all-day toggle ON, and save.
4. Look at how the all-day event renders in day and week views.
custom_expected:
1. The modal contains: name, date, start/end time, an all-day toggle, and a color category.
2. The event saves with the entered values.
3. Re-opening the event shows the saved values.
4. With all-day ON, specific start/end times are not required (the time fields are disabled or hidden).
5. The event is created as an all-day block for that technician and day.

title: Events can be dragged to another technician or another day
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. An event exists on a technician's day.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the event block to a different technician's row.
2. Drag it to a different day.
3. Undo/move back to restore.
custom_expected:
1. Dropping on another technician reassigns the event to them.
2. Dropping on another day moves it to that day.
3. Each move produces a toast with Undo.

title: Event cards are structurally distinct from shift cards - white outlined card with a grey icon chip, no colored left rail
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. An event and a shift sit near each other on the grid.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps: 1. Compare the event card with the shift block side by side.
custom_expected:
1. The event card is a white/neutral card with a thin, even border on all four sides and NO colored left rail (the left rail is the shift's cue).
2. It has a small grey-filled rounded chip on the left containing a calendar icon, and two lines of text beside it: the event name, then the time range in secondary text.
3. The shift reads as a tinted color-filled block with a colored left rail - the two types are separable at a glance, not by color alone.

title: Events default to neutral/grey; choosing a color tints the card and its icon chip
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A newly created event exists with no color chosen.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the new event's default color.
2. Open the event and choose a color from the color picker.
3. Look at the card again.
custom_expected:
1. The default event color is neutral/grey.
2. The color picker offers the same custom color palette as shifts (shared picker with editable labels).
3. Choosing a color tints the card and the icon chip in matching tones, the same way a colored shift is tinted.

title: An event's hours count toward the capacity bar but raise no conflict
refs: SV-8696 (§4.10 (Events),§4.11 (events not conflict-checked),§4.12 (event time included in the utilization total))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Capacity Bars and Events are ON in View Options.
3. A technician has a shift and, on the same day/time, an event (create both, ZZAUTOTEST).
custom_steps:
1. Note the day's capacity bar fill with only the shift present.
2. Add an all-day (or long) event on the same technician and day.
3. Look at the capacity bar again and check for any conflict on the block and in the toolbar conflict pill.
custom_expected:
1. Adding the event DOES increase that day's capacity bar fill - the event's hours are counted alongside shift hours (a 2-hour meeting uses up 2 hours of the technician's available time).
2. The event does NOT create a double-booked or overlap conflict with the shift, and the toolbar conflict count does not increase because of it.
3. The two behave differently on purpose: an event uses up capacity, but it is never flagged as a conflict.

title: Double-booked: two work orders overlapping on the same technician at the same time are flagged
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
  2. Two different work orders have schedulable lines.
  3. You are on the Schedule page; note the toolbar conflict pill's current count.
custom_steps:
1. Schedule work order 1 on a technician for a given time.
  2. Schedule work order 2 on the SAME technician overlapping the same time.
  3. Look at the two blocks and the toolbar conflict pill.
custom_expected:
1. The overlap is detected as a Double-booked conflict.
  2. A warning icon appears on the affected block(s).
  3. The toolbar conflict pill's count increases.
  4. The conflict is listed in the pill's dropdown.

title: Working-day conflict: a shift on a day outside the technician's configured working days is flagged
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician's configured working days are known (for example Monday to Friday); Saturday/Sunday columns are visible (View Options - Saturday and Sunday on).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
custom_steps:
1. Drop the line onto that technician's cell on a day OUTSIDE their working days (for example a Saturday when the technician works Monday to Friday).
2. Look at the block and the conflict pill.
custom_expected:
1. The shift is created but flagged as a conflict because the day is outside the technician's configured working days (the design's reason sentence reads in the spirit of 'Scheduled on a weekend (outside Mon-Fri)').
2. If the technician's working days DO include that day (for example Saturday hours are configured), a shift on that day is NOT flagged.
3. The warning icon appears on the block and the conflict is listed in the toolbar dropdown.

title: Before-hours and after-hours shifts are flagged against the tech's hours
refs: SV-8697 (§4.11 (Before hours,After hours),§4.2 (working-hours hierarchy; 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM default))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician has a known working day (for example 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM).
3. A shift exists for that technician inside those hours.
custom_steps:
1. In day view, drag the shift so it starts BEFORE the technician's working-day start (for example 6:00 AM).
2. Look at the block and the conflict pill.
3. Now drag the shift's right edge so it extends PAST the working-day end (for example to 7:00 PM).
4. Look at the block and the conflict pill again.
custom_expected:
1. The shift is flagged as a before-hours conflict, with a reason sentence in the spirit of 'Starts before working hours', measured against that technician's own configured working-day START time (not a fixed hour).
2. The shift is flagged as an after-hours conflict, with a reason sentence in the spirit of 'Extends past working hours', measured against that technician's own configured working-day END time (not a fixed hour).
3. Both the start and the end follow the hierarchy technician hours, then shop business hours, then the general default working day of 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM.
4. Warning icon on the block in each case; the conflict appears in the toolbar dropdown.

title: The toolbar conflict pill shows the issue count and opens a dropdown listing the conflicts
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. At least two conflicts of different types exist (for example one double-booked overlap and one Saturday shift - create them first).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Read the conflict pill in the grid toolbar.
2. Click it.
3. Read the dropdown.
custom_expected:
1. The pill shows the current number of scheduling issues.
2. Clicking opens a dropdown listing each conflict.
3. The list covers all current conflicts (count matches the pill).
4. Resolving a conflict (for example moving the shift) reduces the count - detection is continuous.

title: Clicking a conflict in the dropdown navigates to the relevant technician and day
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A conflict exists on a technician/day that is NOT currently in view (navigate the grid away first).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open the conflict pill's dropdown.
2. Click the conflict entry.
custom_expected:
1. The grid navigates to the relevant technician and day.
2. The conflicted shift is brought into view.

title: Red/alarming styling is reserved for conflicts and genuine errors - never used for overtime
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. One technician is booked into OVERTIME on a day WITHOUT any conflict (more hours than their day, sequential non-overlapping shifts within working hours - use the technician's working window carefully, or observe the OT tag day).
3. Capacity Bars are on.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the overtime signals for that day ('OT' tag, amber highlights).
2. Look at a conflicted shift for comparison.
custom_expected:
1. Overtime is signaled with the 'OT' text tag and amber tones - NOT red or alarming styling.
2. Red/alarming styling appears only for conflicts and genuine errors.

title: Capacity bar fill = booked (shifts + events) vs available, clamped, equal tracks
refs: SV-8698 (§4.12 (Blue fill - aggregate booked = shifts plus events))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Capacity Bars are ON in View Options (default).
3. Technicians' working hours are known; shifts exist on at least two days with different total booked hours.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Look at each day column's header bar.
2. Compare a lightly-booked day with a heavily-booked day.
3. Compare the bars' track widths across days.
custom_expected:
1. Each day header shows a capacity bar; the blue fill represents total technician-hours booked - shift hours PLUS event hours - divided by total available (sum of all techs' working hours).
2. A more heavily booked day shows a longer blue fill; the fill never exceeds the track (clamped at 100%).
3. The track width is identical across all days (capacity is not rescaled per day), so bars are comparable at a glance.

title: When aggregate hours exceed capacity, an amber spill extends past the track's right edge with a tick at the 100% line
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Capacity Bars are ON.
3. One day is booked BEYOND the team's total available hours (seed extra shifts).
custom_steps: 1. Look at that day's capacity bar.
custom_expected:
1. An amber segment extends past the right edge of the track, showing the excess.
2. A tick marks the 100% line where the track ends.

title: The 'OT' text tag appears whenever any single technician exceeds their own daily hours - even when the day's aggregate is under capacity
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Capacity Bars are ON.
3. On one day, a single technician is booked beyond THEIR daily hours while the team's aggregate for that day remains UNDER total capacity (other techs lightly booked).
custom_steps: 1. Look at that day's capacity bar and header.
custom_expected:
1. An 'OT' tag appears for the day even though the aggregate bar is under 100%.
2. The tag is text, not a color-only signal.
3. Overtime (per-technician) and capacity (aggregate) are independent signals.

title: Hovering a capacity bar shows a per-technician breakdown, with overtime technicians highlighted in amber
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Capacity Bars are ON; a day exists where one technician is in overtime and others are not.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Hover over that day's capacity bar.
2. Read the tooltip.
custom_expected:
1. A tooltip shows a per-technician breakdown: assigned hours vs that technician's capacity.
2. The overtime technician's entry is highlighted in amber.
3. The numbers agree with the shifts actually on the grid.

title: Shift hover tooltip shows customer, unit/vehicle/VIN, date and time, technician, scope, up to 3 line names, and a progress bar
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. A multi-line shift exists covering 5 lines, with some time logged, for a unit that has a VIN.
  3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Hover over the shift block and wait briefly for the tooltip.
  2. Read the tooltip from top to bottom.
custom_expected:
1. The tooltip shows: the customer name; unit, vehicle, and VIN (the tooltip shows the VIN whenever the unit has one, regardless of the 'VIN Number' toggle); the date and time range; the technician; and a scope summary ('N lines · Xh' style).
  2. The individual line names appear as a short list capped at 3, with a '+N more lines' row for the rest (here '+2 more lines'); line statuses are NOT shown.
  3. A time-logged progress bar shows logged vs estimated hours ('X / Yh' style).

title: A conflicted shift's tooltip shows the conflict icon and the conflict reason in amber
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A conflicted shift exists (for example double-booked).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps: 1. Hover the conflicted shift and read the tooltip.
custom_expected:
1. The customer name line includes the conflict icon.
2. The conflict reason is shown in amber.

title: Event hover tooltip shows the event name with its grey category dot, date and time range, and technician
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. An event exists on a technician's day.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps: 1. Hover the event card and read the tooltip.
custom_expected:
1. The tooltip shows the event name with its category dot (grey for a default event).
2. The date and time range are shown.
3. The technician is shown.

title: Tooltips open after a short hover delay, dismiss on mouse-leave, and are read-only - clicking still opens the modal
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A shift exists on the grid.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Move the mouse quickly across the block without stopping - watch for tooltips.
2. Rest the pointer on the block and wait briefly.
3. Move the mouse off the block.
4. Click the block.
custom_expected:
1. A quick pass does not flash tooltips - the tooltip opens only after a short hover delay (spec: roughly 300 to 500ms).
2. It dismisses when the mouse leaves the block.
3. The tooltip is read-only (no buttons/actions inside it).
4. Clicking the block opens the full detail modal as normal.

title: The tooltip flips above the block or shifts horizontally to stay within the viewport - it is never clipped
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-line shift (tall tooltip) exists near the BOTTOM edge of the viewport, and another near a horizontal edge (scroll to arrange).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Hover the shift near the bottom edge and look at where its tooltip opens.
2. Hover the shift near the side edge.
custom_expected:
1. When there is not enough room below, the tooltip opens ABOVE the block instead.
2. Near a side edge, the tooltip shifts horizontally to stay fully within the viewport.
3. No part of the tooltip is clipped off-screen.

title: 'Today' button jumps the grid to the current date
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
  2. You are on the Schedule page, navigated several weeks away from today.
custom_steps:
1. Click the 'Today' button in the grid toolbar.
  2. Look at the grid and the date label.
custom_expected:
1. The grid jumps to the range containing the current date (today's day, this week, or this month depending on the active view).
  2. The date label updates accordingly.

title: Left/right arrows navigate by day, week, or month depending on the active range, and the date label shows the current range
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. In week view, click the right arrow and read the date label.
2. Switch to day view and click the right arrow.
3. Switch to month view and click the left arrow.
custom_expected:
1. Week view: each arrow click moves one whole week; the label shows the week range (spec's example format: 'Jul 14 to 20, 2026').
2. Day view: each click moves one day; the label shows that day.
3. Month view: each click moves one month; the label shows that month.
4. The label always matches what the grid displays.

title: Toolbar search fades non-matching blocks and highlights matching ones (customer, WO number, unit, technician, line name)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Several shifts exist on the visible range for different customers/orders/technicians.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Type a customer name into the toolbar search; look at the grid.
2. Clear, then search a work order number, a unit number, a technician name, and a line name in turn.
3. Clear the search.
custom_expected:
1. Blocks that match the search are highlighted; blocks that do not match fade.
2. All five fields match: customer name, work order number, unit number, technician name, and line name.
3. Matching blocks stay in place on the grid (search visually filters; it does not remove or rearrange).
4. Clearing the search restores all blocks to normal.

title: 'Filter & Display' dropdown combines department toggles, My Shifts, and VIN
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open the 'Filter & Display' dropdown in the grid toolbar.
2. Read its contents and default states.
custom_expected:
1. The dropdown is checkbox style and contains: a toggle per department, 'My Shifts', and 'VIN'.
2. Defaults: all department toggles ON, 'My Shifts' OFF, 'VIN' OFF.
3. There is no separate departments-only control - this dropdown replaces it.

title: Department toggles show or hide individual department groups in the grid
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. At least two department groups are visible in the grid.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. In 'Filter and Display', turn OFF one department's toggle.
2. Look at the grid.
3. Turn it back ON.
custom_expected:
1. The turned-off department's group (header and technician rows) disappears from the grid.
2. Other departments are unaffected.
3. Turning it back on restores the group.

title: 'My Shifts' filters the grid to only the current user's shifts, hiding all other technician rows
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser as a user who appears as a technician row and has at least one shift.
2. Other technicians also have shifts on the visible range.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. In 'Filter and Display', turn ON 'My Shifts'.
2. Look at the grid.
3. Turn it OFF again.
custom_expected:
1. Only shifts assigned to you remain visible; all other technician rows and their shifts are hidden.
2. Turning it off restores the full grid.
3. This is a personal convenience filter only - it does not change what you are permitted to see (default is OFF, everyone's shifts visible).
4. For a user who has no technician/staff record of their own, the 'My Shifts' option is not shown at all.

title: 'VIN Number' toggle gates the block VIN only - tooltip and modal always show it
refs: SV-8700 (§9 (VIN),§4.4); SV-8690 (§4.4,§9 (VIN option)); SV-8694 (§4.8 (Lane height with VIN))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A shift exists for a unit with a VIN; the VIN toggle is OFF.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. With 'VIN Number' off: read the block in week view, hover for the tooltip, then open the detail modal.
2. Turn 'VIN Number' ON in 'Filter and Display'.
3. Read the block again in week view, then in day view, then in month view; hover for the tooltip and open the detail modal again.
4. In day view, compare the height of the shift's lane with the toggle off and on.
custom_expected:
1. 'VIN Number' off: no VIN line on the block (the block shows its three normal lines) - but the hover tooltip still shows the VIN, and the detail modal still shows the VIN.
2. 'VIN Number' on: the VIN appears as an additional line on blocks in day and week views.
