3. Month view blocks never show the VIN, even with the toggle on (space constraints).
4. In day view with the VIN on, the lane height grows to fit the extra VIN line and no block text is clipped or cut off.
5. The 'VIN Number' toggle affects the block only - the tooltip and the modal always show the VIN when the unit has one.

title: 'View Options': six toggles with defaults; Capacity Bars and Events flip
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view with no view options changed yet (fresh state).
3. At least one event and some shifts exist in the visible range, so capacity bars have fill.
custom_steps:
1. Open 'View Options' in the grid toolbar.
2. Read each toggle and its state.
3. Turn OFF Capacity Bars, look at the day column headers, then turn it back ON.
4. Turn OFF Events, look at the grid, then turn it back ON.
custom_expected:
1. Six toggles are offered: Business Hours, Capacity Bars, Events, Tech Hours, Saturday, Sunday.
2. Defaults: Business Hours OFF, Capacity Bars ON, Events ON, Tech Hours OFF, Saturday ON, Sunday ON.
3. Capacity Bars OFF: the capacity bars disappear from the column headers; ON: they reappear with the same values.
4. Events OFF: event blocks disappear from the grid while shifts remain; ON: the events reappear unchanged.

title: Business Hours toggle shades non-working hours in day view
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. The shop has working hours set.
3. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view with Business Hours OFF.
custom_steps:
1. Note the timeline background outside working hours.
2. Turn ON Business Hours in 'View Options'.
3. Look at the timeline again.
custom_expected:
1. With the toggle on, the hours OUTSIDE the working day are shaded with a grey overlay.
2. Working hours remain unshaded.
3. Turning it off removes the shading.

title: Tech Hours toggle displays each technician's working hours next to their name
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Technicians have configured working hours.
3. You are on the Schedule page with Tech Hours OFF (default).
custom_steps:
1. Turn ON Tech Hours in 'View Options'.
2. Look at the technician rows.
custom_expected:
1. Each technician's working hours are displayed next to their name in the row header.
2. The hours match the technicians' configured hours.
3. Turning it off hides the hours again.

title: Saturday and Sunday toggles include or exclude the weekend columns
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page in WEEK view with Saturday and Sunday ON (default) - 7 columns visible.
custom_steps:
1. Turn OFF Saturday in 'View Options'; look at the grid.
2. Turn OFF Sunday too; look again.
3. Turn both back ON.
custom_expected:
1. Saturday off: the Saturday column is removed (6 columns remain).
2. Sunday off too: 5 weekday columns remain (Monday to Friday).
3. Both back on: the full Monday-to-Sunday 7-column week returns.

title: Dragging a shift to another technician row reassigns it - target tech added to the line's roster, source removed, with a confirmation modal
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
  2. A shift exists on technician A; note the affected line's roster.
  3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Drag the shift block from technician A's row to technician B's row.
  2. Confirm the move in the confirmation modal.
  3. Check the line's roster on the work order.
custom_expected:
1. A confirmation modal appears for the cross-technician move.
  2. After confirming, the shift sits on technician B's row.
  3. Technician B is added to the affected line's roster and technician A is removed from it.
  4. A toast with Undo appears.

title: Left-click empty grid space opens a menu: Create Event and New Work Order
refs: SV-8700 (§7 (left-click menu on empty grid space; View Day and New Shift removed),§14.1 (creation via the cell menu))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view (the same menu is offered in month view).
3. Schedulable work order lines exist.
custom_steps:
1. Left-click an empty spot in a technician's grid cell (not on an existing shift or event block).
2. Read the menu items.
custom_expected:
1. A dropdown menu opens at the spot you clicked.
2. It contains ONLY two items: 'Create Event' and 'New Work Order'.
3. There is no 'View Day' item - it was removed from the menu.
4. There is no 'New Shift' item - it was removed from the menu.
5. This menu is opened by a normal left-click - right-clicking the cell does not open it.

title: 'New Work Order' in the cell menu points the user to the Work Orders tab
refs: SV-8700 (§7 / §4.10 New Work Order cell-menu shortcut)
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Schedule grid.
2. The cell menu already shows 'Create Event' and 'New Work Order'.
custom_steps:
1. Left-click an empty spot in a grid cell.
2. Choose 'New Work Order' from the menu.
custom_expected:
1. The menu offers a 'New Work Order' item.
2. Choosing it directs the user to create a work order (a toast / prompt pointing to the Work Orders tab).

title: Deleting a middle shift of a series asks for scope with all three options, each stating the hours returned
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
  2. A series of at least 3 shifts exists for one technician.
  3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete a MIDDLE shift of the series (via the detail modal's Delete).
  2. Read the scope options offered (do not confirm yet).
custom_expected:
1. A scope prompt appears with three options: this shift only, this and everything after, and the whole series.
  2. Each option states its consequence in hours returned (spec's example format: 'returns 8h' / 'returns 56h').
  3. The prompt uses routine, lightweight styling - not alarming destructive styling.

title: 'This shift only' removes that day, the series keeps the gap, and the hours return to the estimate's remaining
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. A series of at least 3 shifts exists; note the total scheduled hours.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete a middle shift with the 'this shift only' scope.
2. Look at the series on the grid.
3. Check the scheduled hours.
custom_expected:
1. Only that day's shift is removed.
2. The series keeps the gap - the remaining shifts do NOT shuffle to close it.
3. The removed day's hours return to the estimate's remaining (scheduled hours drop by that day's hours).
4. An undo toast appears.

title: 'This and everything after' removes from the clicked shift onward, keeping earlier shifts
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. A series of at least 4 shifts exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete the series' THIRD shift with the 'this and everything after' scope.
2. Look at the series on the grid.
custom_expected:
1. The third shift and every later shift of the series are removed.
2. The first two shifts remain untouched.
3. An undo toast appears.

title: 'The whole series' removes all of the series' shifts for that technician
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. The SAME work order has a series on technician A and an independent series on technician B.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete one of technician A's series shifts with the 'whole series' scope.
2. Look at both technicians' rows.
custom_expected:
1. All of technician A's series shifts are removed.
2. Technician B's independent series is untouched (the scope is per technician's series).
3. An undo toast appears.

title: Scope options adapt to position: first and last shifts of a series each show only two options
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. A series of at least 3 shifts exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Start deleting the FIRST shift of the series; read the options, then cancel.
2. Start deleting the LAST shift; read the options, then cancel.
3. Start deleting a MIDDLE shift; read the options, then cancel.
custom_expected:
1. First shift: two options ('this and after' would equal 'whole series', so only two are shown).
2. Last shift: two options ('this and after' would equal 'this only').
3. Middle shift: all three options.
4. Cancelling leaves the series unchanged in every case.

title: Deleting a standalone (non-series) shift does not ask for a series scope
refs: SV-8692 (§7 (derived - scope prompt is for series shifts))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. A single standalone shift (not part of any series) exists.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete the standalone shift.
2. Watch what is asked.
custom_expected:
1. No series-scope prompt appears (the scope question is only for shifts that belong to a series).
2. The shift is deleted and an undo toast appears.

title: Toast lasts ~7s with Undo (about 4s without); stays on hover, goes on leave
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Perform an action that shows a toast (for example move a shift) and let the toast sit untouched - time how long it stays.
2. Trigger another toast and hold the cursor OVER it well past its normal lifetime.
3. Move the cursor off the toast.
custom_expected:
1. Untouched, a toast that has an Undo action persists about 7 seconds; a toast without Undo persists about 4 seconds, before dismissing.
2. While the cursor is over it, the toast stays (does not auto-dismiss).
3. After the cursor leaves, it dismisses.

title: Every create/delete/move/reassign toasts with Undo, and Undo restores
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. Schedulable lines exist and a shift exists; note its technician, day, and time.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Create a shift and watch for the toast.
2. Delete the shift, watch for the toast, then click Undo on it.
3. Move the shift to another day, watch for the toast, then click Undo.
4. Reassign it to another technician, watch for the toast, then click Undo.
5. Check the line's roster after the reassign undo.
custom_expected:
1. Each of the four actions (create, delete, move, reassign) produces a toast notification, and every toast offers an Undo option.
2. Undo after delete: the shift is back exactly where it was.
3. Undo after move: the shift returns to its original day/time.
4. Undo after reassign: the shift returns to the original technician, and the line's roster is restored (original tech back on, target tech off).
5. Every destructive action is undoable within the toast's lifetime.

title: Schedule actions save immediately - Undo reverses them, closing does not cancel
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. A shift exists on the grid; note its technician, day, and time.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete the shift. While the Undo toast is still showing, refresh the page WITHOUT clicking Undo.
2. Check the grid for the shift.
3. Recreate a shift, move it to another day, and again refresh while the toast shows, without clicking Undo.
4. Finally do one more delete and this time click Undo before the toast disappears.
custom_expected:
1. The delete took effect immediately: after the refresh the shift is gone even though Undo was never clicked - closing or refreshing does not cancel the action.
2. The move also stuck after the refresh - the shift is on the new day.
3. Clicking Undo within the toast's lifetime reverses the action (the deleted shift comes back).
4. Note for the tester: Undo works by performing a reversing action, not by holding the change back - a change surviving a refresh before Undo is expected, not a bug.

title: Escape closes the topmost open modal or popover, following the stacking order
refs: SV-8700 (§7 (Keyboard support - Escape,including within the shift modal))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open the shift detail modal, then open the color picker inside it and press Escape.
2. Open the time picker inside the modal and press Escape; then start editing a note and press Escape.
3. With nothing open inside the modal, press Escape again.
4. Open the shift detail modal again with a popover from elsewhere on top of it, and press Escape twice.
custom_expected:
1. Escape with the color picker open closes only the color picker - the modal stays open.
2. Same for the time picker and the note edit - each sub-picker closes first and the modal stays open.
3. Escape with no open sub-picker closes the modal itself.
4. With two layers open, the FIRST Escape closes only the topmost layer, and the SECOND Escape closes the next layer down.
5. Escape works anywhere on the schedule page as a global shortcut, following the defined stacking order (delete scope, reassign, spread, capacity, event modal, event view, line picker, shift detail, cell menu, calendar picker, customize, filters, search).

title: Enter confirms the active dialog, but not inside a note textarea
refs: SV-8700 (§7 (Keyboard support - Enter; Enter does not fire inside textareas))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Delete.
2. Shifts/series and events exist to exercise the dialogs.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open the spread step for a large job, press Enter.
2. Open the reassign dialog for a shift, choose a technician, press Enter.
3. Open the event modal with valid fields, press Enter.
4. Open a series delete-scope prompt, select a scope, press Enter.
5. Open a shift's detail modal, click into the note editor, type a line of note text and press Enter, then type a second line.
custom_expected:
1. In each confirmable dialog, Enter confirms it - equivalent to clicking its confirm action.
2. The confirmed action takes effect (spread created / reassigned / event saved / delete applied).
3. In the note editor, Enter inserts a new line in the note - it does NOT confirm or close the dialog.
4. The multiline note can be completed and saved normally.

title: Modals trap focus and all interactive elements are keyboard-reachable
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift's detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Press Tab repeatedly and watch where focus goes.
2. Continue tabbing past the last control in the modal.
3. Close the modal and Tab through the schedule page's toolbar and sidebar controls.
custom_expected:
1. Focus moves through the modal's interactive elements with visible focus rings.
2. Focus stays trapped inside the modal (wraps back to its first control) until the modal closes.
3. On the page, toolbar and sidebar controls are reachable by keyboard.

title: Blue is the default color for all shifts, including long and multi-week jobs
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
  2. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Create a normal single-day shift without touching any color option.
  2. Create a multi-week series without touching any color option.
  3. Look at both on the grid.
custom_expected:
1. Both the single shift and the multi-week series render in the default blue.
  2. No special color is auto-applied to long jobs - blue is the default for ALL shifts.

title: Shift modal color picker recolors that shift only, in matching tones
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Two shifts from the SAME work order exist (for example on different technicians).
3. One of those shifts' detail modal is open.
custom_steps:
1. Open the color picker in the modal.
2. Choose a non-default color.
3. Look at the block on the grid.
4. Compare that shift with the other shift from the same work order.
custom_expected:
1. The shift's block re-renders in the chosen color.
2. The color provides three consistent tones: background fill, text color, and accent (left border).
3. The color is per SHIFT, not per work order - the other shift from the same work order keeps its own (default blue) color and does not change.
4. Colors carry no fixed meaning - they are free choice beyond the two defaults (blue shift / grey event).

title: Color labels are editable per shop
refs: SV-8700 (§10 (Color labels are editable per shop),§4.10 (shared picker))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shift's or event's color picker is open.
custom_steps:
1. Find the editable label of one color in the picker.
2. Rename it (for example to 'ZZAUTOTEST Rush').
3. Open the picker again from another shift/event.
4. Restore the original label.
custom_expected:
1. Each color's label can be edited.
2. The renamed label shows for the whole shop - the same picker opened elsewhere shows 'ZZAUTOTEST Rush'.
3. Shifts and events share the same custom palette with the same labels.

title: Schedule: View grants the full read experience - page, all three views, mini calendar, search, filter, tooltips, read-only modals
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule: View but NOT Edit (assign a suitable system role or a purpose-made custom role; restore after).
  2. Shifts and events exist on the grid, created by an Edit-capable user.
  3. You are signed in AS that View-only user on a desktop browser.
custom_steps:
1. Open the Schedule page.
  2. Switch between Day, Week, and Month.
  3. Use the mini calendar, the toolbar search, and the sidebar filter.
  4. Hover a shift for its tooltip, then click it to open the detail modal.
custom_expected:
1. The Schedule page opens and all three views work.
  2. The mini calendar, search, and filters all work.
  3. ALL technicians' shifts and events are visible (not just the user's own).
  4. Tooltips show on hover, and the shift/event detail modals open in read-only mode.

title: View-only: every editing affordance is hidden or disabled
refs: SV-8685 (§14.1 (Schedule: View - editing affordances hidden or disabled))
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule: View but NOT Edit.
2. Shifts, a series, and events exist on the grid.
3. You are signed in AS that View-only user on a desktop browser, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Look for drag handles on sidebar lines and try to drag a work order card onto the grid.
2. Try dragging an existing shift block (move/reassign) and look for resize handles in day view.
3. Left-click an empty spot in a grid cell.
4. Open a shift's detail modal and inspect its fields and actions.
custom_expected:
1. No drag handles are offered and nothing can be dragged from the sidebar onto the grid.
2. Shift blocks cannot be moved or resized - no drop targets or resize handles appear.
3. No creation menu opens at all - there is no 'Create Event' and no 'New Work Order' offered.
4. In the modal, edit fields are hidden or disabled, and the reassign and delete actions are absent.

title: With Schedule: View OFF, the Schedule top-level nav item is hidden entirely
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule: View OFF (no Schedule permission).
2. You are signed in AS that user on a desktop browser.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the app's main navigation.
2. Search the nav for any Schedule entry.
custom_expected:
1. The Schedule top-level nav item is not shown at all.
2. The rest of the app works normally for the role.

title: Schedule: Edit unlocks all creation and modification interactions
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule: Edit (and View) but NOT Delete.
2. Work orders with approved lines exist; you are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Drag a work order from the sidebar onto a technician cell and complete the scope picker (and spread modal for a large job).
2. Left-click an empty spot in a cell and create an event via 'Create Event'; do the same on the timeline in day view.
3. Reassign a shift between technicians by dragging.
4. In day view, edge-resize and horizontally drag a shift.
5. Edit fields in the shift and event detail modals.
custom_expected:
1. Drag-and-drop from the sidebar, the scope picker, and the spread modal all work.
2. Shift and event creation works, including via the menu opened by left-clicking empty grid space in both week and day view.
3. Reassignment between technicians works.
4. Edge-resize and horizontal drag work in day view.
5. Modal fields are editable and save.

title: Edit without Delete: the user can create and modify but cannot remove - delete action and trash icon hidden
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule: Edit but NOT Delete.
2. A shift, a series, and an event exist (some created by this user).
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Open a shift's detail modal and look for the delete action / trash icon.
2. Open an event's modal and look for a delete action.
3. Try to find ANY way to remove a shift or event.
custom_expected:
1. The delete action and the trash icon are hidden in the shift modal.
2. Events likewise offer no delete.
3. No path exists to remove shifts or events - while creating and modifying still work.

title: Schedule: Delete unlocks deleting shifts and events, including the three series-aware scopes
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule: Delete.
2. A standalone shift, a series, and an event exist.
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Delete the standalone shift.
2. Delete a series shift and read the scope options.
3. Delete the event.
custom_expected:
1. The delete action is available and works for shifts.
2. Series deletion offers its scopes (this shift / this and after / whole series).
3. Events can be deleted too.
4. Undo toasts appear (restore the items via Undo to clean up).

title: The permission tiers depend on each other: Delete requires Edit, and Edit requires View
refs: SV-8685 (§14 (Delete requires Edit and Edit requires View))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an admin who can edit custom roles.
2. A ZZAUTOTEST custom role exists (create one; delete after).
custom_steps:
1. In the role's Schedule permissions, try to enable Edit while View is off.
2. Try to enable Delete while Edit is off.
3. Enable View, then Edit, then Delete in order.
custom_expected:
1. Edit cannot be granted without View (the admin UI enforces or auto-selects the dependency).
2. Delete cannot be granted without Edit.
3. The three tiers can be enabled in dependency order, so each higher level always includes the ones beneath it (Delete includes Edit, and Edit includes View).

title: Schedule access without Work Orders: View - sidebar hides the WO list and drill-down; mini calendar stays; grid shifts remain usable
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule access but Work Orders: View OFF.
2. Shifts already exist on the grid.
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Look at the left sidebar.
2. Interact with the shifts already on the grid (hover, open modal, and - if the role has Edit - move one).
3. Try to find any way to drag a new work order onto the grid.
custom_expected:
1. The sidebar hides the work order list and the line drill-down; the mini calendar remains available.
2. Shifts already on the grid can still be viewed and interacted with per the role's Schedule tier.
3. New work orders cannot be dragged on - the WO list is simply not visible.

title: No own-only restriction: every Schedule: View user sees ALL technicians' shifts and events
custom_preconds:
1. Shifts and events exist for SEVERAL different technicians.
2. A test user with a low-tier View-only role exists (and is themselves one of the technicians).
3. You are signed in AS that user, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Read the grid across all departments and technicians.
2. Check 'My Shifts' in 'Filter and Display' is OFF (default).
custom_expected:
1. The user sees ALL technicians' shifts and events, not only their own - there is no role-based 'own shifts only' restriction.
2. 'My Shifts' exists only as an optional personal convenience filter (off by default), not a security boundary.

title: Grid rows are department-based: any staff member in a visible department appears as a row, regardless of role
custom_preconds:
1. A staff member with a NON-technician role (for example Office) is assigned to a department that is visible on the schedule (set up; restore after).
2. Another staff member has NO department assignment.
3. You are signed in on a desktop browser, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Look for the department-assigned Office staff member among the grid rows.
2. Look for the staff member with no department.
custom_expected:
1. The department-assigned staff member appears as a technician row - row presence is controlled by the department on the staff record, NOT by role permission.
2. The staff member without a department does not appear as a row.

title: Clocking into work order line tasks is gated by the staff record's 'Time Clock' setting, not the permission model
custom_preconds:
1. Two staff members exist: one with the 'Time Clock' setting ON on their staff record, one with it OFF (set up; restore after).
2. Both appear as schedule rows and have shifts on work order lines.
custom_steps:
1. As (or with) the Time-Clock-ON staff member, attempt to clock into their work order line task.
2. As (or with) the Time-Clock-OFF staff member, attempt the same.
custom_expected:
1. The Time-Clock-ON staff member can clock in.
2. The Time-Clock-OFF staff member cannot - the ability is controlled by the staff-record setting, not by the Schedule permission tier.

title: With Work Orders: View OFF, work-order-derived details on shifts (customer, lines, money fields) are hidden or masked
custom_preconds:
1. A test user's role has Schedule access but Work Orders: View OFF (assign a suitable role; restore after).
2. Shifts already exist on the grid, created by a fully-permissioned user, for units that have customers, scheduled lines, and a VIN.
3. You are signed in AS that user on a desktop browser, on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Look at a shift block on the grid and read its text lines.
2. Hover the shift for its tooltip.
3. Open the shift's detail modal and read the work-order-derived fields.
custom_expected:
1. Work-order-derived details (customer, the scheduled line list, and any money-bearing fields) are hidden or masked wherever they would normally appear - on the block, in the tooltip, and in the modal.
2. The schedule structure itself (the shift's day, time, and technician) stays visible so the grid remains usable.
3. This extends the sidebar behavior (the work order list and drill-down are hidden) to the work-order data surfaced on the shifts themselves.

title: Below 960px the grid scrolls horizontally, and the sidebar collapses on narrow viewports
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view with shifts visible.
custom_steps:
1. Resize the browser window to just under 960px wide.
2. Try to reach the right-hand days of the grid.
3. Narrow the window further and watch the sidebar.
custom_expected:
1. Below the 960px minimum supported width, the grid scrolls horizontally rather than breaking.
2. All days remain reachable by horizontal scroll.
3. On narrow viewports the sidebar collapses.
4. No content becomes permanently unreachable and nothing errors.

title: The sidebar work order list and line drill-down stay smooth with 50+ items
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. 50 or more open work orders exist (seed ZZAUTOTEST orders if the environment lacks them), including one order with many approved lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
custom_steps:
1. Scroll the full work order list top to bottom quickly.
2. Open the many-line order's drill-down and scroll it.
3. Type in the search while the long list is shown.
custom_expected:
1. Scrolling stays smooth with no long freezes or blank stretches that fail to fill in (the list virtualizes at 50+ items).
2. The drill-down behaves the same with many lines.
3. Search stays responsive on the long list.

title: The grid renders smoothly at full load - 15 technicians × 7 days with several shifts per cell
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. The schedule is loaded to roughly the spec's stated scale: around 15 technician rows across a week with several shifts per cell (seed ZZAUTOTEST shifts as needed).
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
custom_steps:
1. Scroll the grid vertically and horizontally.
2. Switch between Day, Week, and Month.
3. Hover several blocks and open/close a modal.
custom_expected:
1. The grid renders and scrolls smoothly at this scale.
2. View switches complete without long hangs.
3. Tooltips and modals stay responsive.

title: Shop closures do NOT block spread in V1 - shifts can land on closure days
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A shop closure (holiday/inventory day) is defined at the shop level on a working weekday inside the planned spread window (set it up; remove after).
3. A large job (multi-day scope) is ready to spread.
custom_steps:
1. Open the spread step across a window that contains a shop closure day.
2. Expand the preview and find the closure day.
3. Confirm the spread and check the grid.
custom_expected:
1. The closure day is NOT struck through or skipped by the spread in V1.
2. A shift CAN be placed on the shop closure day (only weekend days with no business hours are skipped).
3. The end date follows the normal daily distribution - no extra day is added for the closure.

title: Scheduled hours, the estimate, and actual (clocked) hours are three separate quantities that are not forced to reconcile
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A line has estimate 10h; a technician has 6h scheduled against it and some different amount of time actually clocked (seed what is possible).
custom_steps:
1. Open the shift's detail modal.
2. Compare the scheduled hours, the estimate, and the logged/actual time.
custom_expected:
1. All three quantities are shown/derivable and may differ from one another.
2. Nothing forces them to match - no error, no auto-correction (progress is driven by clocked-in time).

title: A multi-week series keeps the same local start time across the clock change
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. The shop's location observes daylight saving (clocks change); the next clock-change date is known (e.g. the November change).
3. A job large enough to spread across the clock-change date exists.
custom_steps:
1. Spread the job across a window that includes the clock-change date (shifts before and after it).
2. Open shifts from before the change and from after the change and read their start times.
custom_expected:
1. Every shift in the series starts at the SAME local wall-clock time (e.g. 8:00 AM) on both sides of the clock change.
2. No shift in the series silently moves an hour earlier or later after the change date.

title: Schedule and all its dialogs display correctly in dark mode
refs: SV-8685 (§11 (Dark theme - user-selectable Light / Dark,persisted per user))
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on a desktop browser; the app's dark mode / theme toggle is available.
2. The Schedule page has shifts, an event, a conflict, and capacity bars visible.
custom_steps:
1. Switch the app to dark mode.
2. Look over the Schedule grid: shift blocks, event cards, capacity bars, conflict styling, tooltips.
3. Open each dialog/popover you can reach (shift detail, event form, spread step, delete scope, filters, view options).
4. Switch back to light mode and spot-check again.
custom_expected:
1. In dark mode every part of the Schedule stays readable - no white-on-white or black-on-black text, no unreadable labels or invisible icons.
2. Every dialog and popover opened from the Schedule follows the dark theme too.
3. Conflict and overtime cues remain distinguishable (they never rely on colour alone - text/icon still present).
4. Switching back to light mode restores the normal look with nothing stuck in dark colours.

title: Business-hours toggle reveals a per-day (Mon-Sun) From-To editor
refs: SV-8699 (§4.2 Working Hours - business hours toggle,per-day From/To editor)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App with access to location settings.
2. You are on the Edit Location screen for a shop.
custom_steps:
1. Find the business hours setting on Edit Location and read its default state.
2. Turn the 'Set business hours for this shop' toggle ON.
3. Read the per-day rows shown when business hours are ON.
4. Set a From time and a To time for one day (for example Monday).
5. Save the location settings.
custom_expected:
1. Edit Location shows a toggle labelled 'Set business hours for this shop', and it is OFF by default (no business hours set).
2. Turning it ON reveals a per-day working-hours editor for the shop.
3. There is one row per day of the week, Monday through Sunday.
4. Each day has a From time and a To time you can set.
5. The saved shop business hours are used by the Schedule (start-time hierarchy, before/after-hours conflicts, business-hours shading).

title: Edit Staff has a 'Set custom hours for this technician' toggle, off by default
refs: SV-8699 (§4.2 Working Hours - technician custom-hours toggle)
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with access to staff settings.
2. You open the Edit Staff Member screen for a technician.
custom_steps:
1. Open the Edit Staff Member screen for a technician.
2. Find the custom-hours setting and read its default state.
3. Turn the 'Set custom hours for this technician' toggle ON.
custom_expected:
1. Edit Staff Member shows a toggle labelled 'Set custom hours for this technician'.
2. The toggle is OFF by default (no custom hours set).
3. Turning it ON reveals a per-day working-hours editor for that technician.

title: A technician with no custom hours inherits the shop business hours
refs: SV-8699 (§4.2 Working Hours - inherit shop hours when no custom hours)
custom_preconds:
1. The shop has business hours set (/02).
2. A technician has the 'Set custom hours for this technician' toggle OFF.
custom_steps:
1. Confirm the technician has no custom hours set.
2. Schedule a shift for that technician and check start-time defaults / before-after-hours conflicts against the shop business hours.
custom_expected:
1. With no custom hours, the technician's working hours fall back to the shop business hours.
2. Start-time defaults and before/after-hours conflict checks for that technician use the shop business hours.

title: 'Add hours' appends a removable second range for split shifts, starting empty
refs: SV-8699 (§4.2 Working Hours - Add hours split shifts)
custom_preconds: 1. You are in the per-day working-hours editor (location or technician) with a day's first range set.
custom_steps:
1. On one day, click 'Add hours'.
2. Read the new range that appears.
3. Set the second range, then remove it.
custom_expected:
1. 'Add hours' appends an additional From-To range to that day (to support split shifts).
2. The added range starts empty (no From/To pre-filled).
3. Each added range can be removed individually.

title: Overlapping hour ranges block Save; incomplete rows are ignored
refs: SV-8699 (§4.2 Working Hours - overlap validation; incomplete rows ignored by overlap check)
custom_preconds: 1. You are in the per-day working-hours editor with at least two ranges on one day.
custom_steps:
1. Set two ranges on the same day so their times overlap.
2. Look at the offending range and the Save button.
3. Fix the overlap, then on one day add another range and leave its From and/or To empty.
4. Look at the validation state and the Save button again.
custom_expected:

2. An inline message reads 'These hours overlap. Adjust the times so they don't conflict.'
3. Save is disabled while the overlap exists.
4. The incomplete row (empty From/To) is ignored by the overlap check - it does not raise the overlap error.
5. Save is not blocked by an incomplete row on its own (only genuine overlaps disable Save).

title: Week Export opens a printable Department-by-Technician week grid
refs: SV-8685 (design Week Export - V1 scope pending Branko)
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Schedule screen in Week view with some shifts scheduled.
2. Your role has Schedule: View.
custom_steps:
1. Open the Week Export / Print action for the current week.
2. Read the exported / printable layout.
3. Check the department grouping, the technician rows, and the shifts shown per day.
custom_expected:

2. It is formatted for printing (a clean page layout, without the interactive grid controls).
3. The exported view groups technicians by department, with department headers.
4. Each technician's shifts for the week appear in the correct day columns.
5. The week's date range is shown.

title: Shifts and events created before the Schedule rewrite still appear after it
custom_preconds:
1. This case runs around the Schedule rewrite release: before the release, note (or create) a handful of scheduled shifts and calendar events - including at least one future-dated one - with their technician, day, and time.
2. The release (which replaces the Schedule behind the scenes) has been deployed.
custom_steps:
1. After the release, open the Schedule and navigate to the dates of the noted entries.
2. Compare each noted shift and event against what the grid now shows.
3. Open a couple of them to check their details.
custom_expected:
